analysis:
Examined the base text of provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Protocol/Messages.swift (lines 653-1716) and the patch excerpt. The PR adds an optional `busy: ProviderBusy?` field to Register and Heartbeat, with encode/decode wiring at head lines ~948-951, 1070, 1097, 1345-1346 and 1371-1372. The field is provider-to-coordinator only and carries a busy reason, a since-timestamp and an add-on identifier. It is additive and omitted when nil, and it touches no key material, no attestation or App Attest fields, and no prompt or ciphertext paths. The prefix-cache receipt paths (T-041) are unchanged in the visible base text: readyAnchors is still capped at 16 via suffix(16), and the receipt types are untouched.

Security-relevant observations for later passes:
1. The `busy` metadata is self-reported by the provider (ADV-001). The coordinator must treat it only as an advisory routing exclusion. It must not let `busy` or `draining` alter authorization or trust (TB-011, T-052/T-053). The coordinator side is outside the supplied evidence.
2. The `busy_reason` and `busy_addon` strings are provider-controlled and unbounded as far as the visible text shows. The coordinator or consumer UI must sanitize and size-limit them. The ProviderBusy type definition is not in the supplied units, so I cannot verify field bounds or that it excludes prompt-derived content. The decoder also admits an inbound heartbeat with this field.
3. The Register `busy` field would be sent before attestation completes, but it only excludes the provider from routing, so it does not widen trust.

The patch excerpt is truncated, and the ProviderBusy definition and the head-side encode/decode bodies were not visible. I therefore could not confirm there is no prompt leakage or unbounded content in `busy`, and I report no regression.
